summary.headline: Laurus FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR6,813 crore and EBITDA margin hit 26.8%, with Q4 margin at 28.9%; FY27 capex guided to about INR3,000 crore over two years.
summary.overview: FY26 was a strong year: revenue of INR6,813 crore (+23%), gross margin about 60.4%, EBITDA of INR1,826 crore (26.8% margin, +6.7 pp) and PAT of INR889 crore (+148%). Q4 revenue grew only 5% YoY to INR1,812 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin reached 28.9% on operating leverage and better mix. CDMO grew about 38% in small molecules to INR1,896 crore, while Affordable Medicines (formerly Generics) grew 18% to INR4,733 crore. Management raised its multi-year capex expectation sharply, to around INR3,000 crore over the next two years from the earlier INR1,000 crore a year reference, and the call stressed CDMO share rising to 50% by FY30.

segments.name: Small molecule CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,896 crore (+38%); Q4 sales about INR524 crore. Growth came from late-stage programs, commercial NCE API supplies and ramp-up of growth projects.

segments.name: Total CDMO (incl. Bio)
segments.commentary: Full-year CDMO business a little over INR2,000 crore (INR2,080 crore), above 30% of revenue versus 13% six years ago.

segments.name: Laurus Bio
segments.commentary: Q4 sales about INR65 crore (+124% YoY on a low base); FY26 sales up about 15%. Phase 1 fermentation capacity at Vizag due by end-2026.

segments.name: Affordable Medicines (formerly Generics)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,223 crore with growth moderating; FY26 revenue INR4,733 crore (+18%), driven by ARV and oncology volumes and developed-market launches.

segments.name: ARV
segments.commentary: FY26 ARV revenue about INR2,800 crore, versus the INR2,500 crore plus or minus 200 crore run-rate previously cited; ARV now 41% of revenue, down from 67% six years ago. Mix is about two-thirds API and one-third formulations.

guidance_outlook: Capex guidance raised to about INR3,000 crore over the next two years, from the INR1,000 crore a year reference; one analyst's question cited INR1,500 crore a year.
Gross debt may rise slightly in FY27, but debt/EBITDA is expected to hold at or soften from 1.25x.
Effective tax rate around 25-26%; standalone at 25%.
Management is confident of maintaining or improving the roughly 29% EBITDA margin in FY27 and expects operating leverage next year.
Expects good YoY CDMO growth in FY27 with possible quarter-to-quarter lumpiness; Affordable Medicines order book in place for strong FY27 growth, with no quantitative guidance.
CDMO expected to reach 50% of sales by FY30; ARV revenue stays around INR2,800 crore but its share falls.
R&D spend to stay around 4.1% of sales in FY27.
capex_capacity: Unit 7 greenfield manufacturing: first production ready for commercial validation by March 2027; four more manufacturing units in FY28, adding over 2,000 cubic metres of reactor volume.
Commercial-scale peptide manufacturing block ready for validation in Q2 FY27; management declined to give peptide capex or capacity numbers.

Laurus Bio fermentation greenfield at Vizag: Phase 1 operational by end-2026. Bangalore R2 is fully occupied (4 x 45,000 litre fermenters); 250,000 litres now, another 400,000 litres by year-end, with room for 600,000 more.
KRKA JV formulation facility in Hyderabad: Phase 1 by mid-2027.
Formulation capacity up 20% to 12 billion units in FY26; a new tertiary packaging/formulation facility is due in June for an existing 3-billion-tablet CMO partner.
Company exceeded 8,200 cubic metres of small-molecule reactor volume in FY26. Asset turnover 0.89x.
demand_pricing: ARV pricing was broadly constant in FY26; higher ARV sales were driven by full utilisation of ARV assets.
Gross margin gain was attributed to softer raw-material prices and process improvements, with better product mix.
Q4 saw some solvent price pressure, but management said production is not affected and it expects no disruption through June; some pressure expected, offset by higher utilisation.
Management said the three recent commercial APIs have multi-year patent life and partner forecasts, and it sees no destocking risk; it also said there is no single-product concentration.
Geopolitical disruption may pressure raw-material availability, logistics and OTIF performance across the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Is there product concentration or destocking risk in the CDMO book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said three commercial APIs delivered in the last 18 months have multi-year patent life and clear partner forecasts; no destocking seen and no single-product dependence.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage drive margins beyond gross margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects operating leverage next year as capacity utilisation rises; Q4 EBITDA margin was near 29% and rose through each quarter of FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag fermentation: yield variability and ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial Vizag batches are industrial chemicals, surfactants and polymers (non-pharma); contamination is the main risk, and products are moving from 45 KL to 110 KL fermenters after commercial gates were cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ARV API/formulation split and non-ARV formulation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds API and one-third formulations for FY26 overall; non-ARV formulations are growing with momentum expected into FY27 from existing products.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARV share fall, and what is the CDMO target?
qa_highlights.answer: ARV stays around INR2,800 crore in absolute terms but its share falls; CDMO is targeted at 50% of sales by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capex raised, and what are return expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says capex is growth-led with visibility on customer and product, and expects about INR3,000 crore over two years.

risks_watch: Q4 revenue growth slowed to 5% YoY even as margins expanded; watch whether revenue growth resumes in FY27.
Solvent and raw-material price pressure and geopolitical supply risk; management expects some pressure but claims stable margins.
Capex step-up to about INR3,000 crore over two years with slightly higher gross debt in FY27; watch return ratios and utilisation of new capacity.
CDMO lumpiness quarter to quarter; a peer with destocking challenges was cited.
Affordable Medicines growth moderating; FY27 growth not quantified.
Customer-specific items (an Amplia Therapeutics project, crop science, electronics/OLED with LORDIN) were not quantified; management declined comment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, margins and capex visibility, with a firm stance on maintaining gross margin and the 29% EBITDA level. Evasive on quantitative detail: they declined to give peptide capex, customer advances, CDMO development-versus-commercial split, Affordable Medicines growth percentage and timing for the Atchutapuram greenfield project.
key_quotes: Our business model has proven as resilient, and we remain well positioned to execute on our growth strategy ahead.
We are very confident on maintaining or improving this EBITDA margin in FY '27.
So fortunately, we haven't had any challenges so far.
Most of the capex what we're doing is growth capex.

growth.why: Management guides to maintaining or improving ~29% EBITDA margin in FY27 and good CDMO growth, backed by Bangalore R2 fully occupied, Unit 7 validation by March 2027, Laurus Bio Vizag Phase 1 by end-2026, and a raised ~INR3,000 crore two-year capex plan, though no quantitative FY27 revenue growth was given and peptide and peptide capex numbers were not disclosed.
